reno.q: In what year did Reno first raise a steel arch over Virginia Street?
reno.why: The first arch went up on October 23, 1926.

reno.q: An entrant from Sacramento won $100 for writing what?
o: The slogan "The Biggest Little City in the World"
The name of the Truckee River bridge
reno.why: The slogan contest followed the 1927 highways exposition.

reno.q: Who built the first bridge at this crossing in 1860?
reno.why: Charles Fuller built it in 1860. Myron Lake took over in 1861 and charged tolls.

reno.q: Which California town received the 1963 arch?
reno.why: The arch went to Willits, which changed its slogan to welcome visitors to the redwoods.

vc.q: In what year was silver found at Virginia City?
vc.why: Silver was found in 1859, setting off the Comstock Lode rush.

vc.q: Which newspaper did young Sam Clemens write for in Virginia City?
vc.why: He wrote for the Territorial Enterprise and first signed "Mark Twain" in 1863.

vc.q: What happened in Virginia City on October 26, 1875?
vc.why: The Great Fire burned much of the town and left about 2,000 people homeless.

vc.q: In what year did the last class graduate from the Fourth Ward School?
vc.why: The last class graduated in 1936. The building reopened as a museum in 1986.

tahoeicons.why: Lora Josephine Knight built it, with the architect Lennart Palme.

tahoeicons.q: What is the only island in Lake Tahoe called?
tahoeicons.why: Fannette Island sits in Emerald Bay.

tahoeicons.q: In what year did the Sand Harbor park have its grand opening?
tahoeicons.why: Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park held its grand opening in 1971.

tahoeicons.q: Camp Richardson is named after whom?
tahoeicons.why: Captain Alonzo L. Richardson started a stage service here in 1921.

tahoe.q: Which river leaves Lake Tahoe at Fanny Bridge?
tahoe.why: The Truckee River is the lake's only outlet.

tahoe.q: In what year was the present concrete Lake Tahoe Dam finished?
When did the original gatekeeper's cabin burn?
tahoe.why: It burned in 1978. The present cabin was finished in 1981.

tahoe.q: For whom did Robert Watson build his log cabin in 1908?
tahoe.why: He built it for his son and daughter-in-law, who moved in during 1909.

boston.q: In what year was the Old State House completed?
boston.why: It is the city's oldest surviving public building.

boston.q: How did the town vote on accepting Faneuil's market in 1740?
o: It was decided by a coin flip
boston.why: The vote was 367 to 360, so it was very close.

boston.q: In what year did Paul Revere buy his house?
boston.why: He bought it on January 13, 1770, and owned it until 1800.

boston.q: How many lanterns were hung in the Old North Church steeple on April 18, 1775?
boston.why: Two lanterns warned patriots in Charlestown that the British were moving by water.

dc.q: In what year was the Lincoln Memorial dedicated?
Work on the Washington Monument stopped in 1854. When did it resume?
dc.why: Work stopped from 1854 until 1877 because of money problems and the Civil War.

dc.q: In what year did British troops burn the Capitol?
dc.why: British troops burned it on August 24, 1814, during the War of 1812.

dc.q: When was the bronze statue of Jefferson installed?
dc.why: A plaster statue stood there in 1943. The bronze one arrived in April 1947.

ny.q: Who helped supervise the Brooklyn Bridge construction for about 11 years after Washington Roebling became too ill to visit?
ny.why: Emily Warren Roebling relayed communications and managed daily work.

ny.q: When did Grand Central Terminal open?
What was the Flatiron Building first called?
ny.why: It was named for George A. Fuller, founder of the Fuller Company.

ny.q: Whose company built the iron frame inside the Statue of Liberty?
ny.why: Gustave Eiffel's company built the frame. Bartholdi was the sculptor.

chicago.q: How many stainless steel plates make up Cloud Gate?
What did the Chicago Water Tower's castle look hide?
o: A standpipe that smoothed water pressure
chicago.why: It was a standpipe added in 1869.

chicago.q: The sea horses at Buckingham Fountain stand for what?
o: The four states that touch Lake Michigan

chicago.q: How was the Chicago Theatre promoted when it opened in 1921?
chicago.why: It opened on October 26, 1921, promoted as the Wonder Theatre of the World.

sf.q: What is the Golden Gate Bridge's official color called?
In what year did the Ferry Building open?
Lillie Hitchcock Coit left money for what purpose?
o: Adding to the beauty of the city

sf.q: Why was the Palace of Fine Arts rebuilt in concrete?
sf.why: It was built of plaster over wood for the 1915 fair and decayed.

philly.q: Which document was drafted at Independence Hall in 1787?
philly.why: The Constitutional Convention met May 25 to September 17, 1787.

philly.q: Who gave the Liberty Bell its famous name in the 1830s?
philly.why: Abolitionist societies called it the Liberty Bell.

philly.q: The Betsy Ross flag story traces back mostly to whom?
philly.why: Historians trace it to her grandsons, the Canbys, and the Centennial.

philly.q: Elfreth's Alley is called the nation's oldest what?
philly.why: Wikipedia calls it our nation's oldest residential street.

la.q: Who donated the land for Griffith Observatory?
la.why: Griffith J. Griffith donated 3,015 acres in 1896.

la.q: What did the Hollywood Sign originally read?
la.why: It advertised the Hollywoodland housing development in 1923.

la.q: Which film opened Grauman's Chinese Theatre in 1927?
la.why: It opened May 18, 1927 with DeMille's The King of Kings.

seattle.q: What was the Space Needle built for?
seattle.why: It opened April 21, 1962 for the Century 21 Exposition.

seattle.q: Who is the bronze pig at Pike Place Market named?
seattle.why: Rachel is a 550-pound bronze piggy bank.

seattle.q: Smith Tower was the tallest building west of the Mississippi until which year?
seattle.why: The Kansas City Power & Light Building passed it in 1931.

seattle.q: What did Gas Works Park used to be?
seattle.why: A coal gasification plant ran there from 1906 to 1956.

nola.q: When did Jackson Square get its current name?
nola.why: It kept the name Place d'Armes until 1851.

nola.q: What destroyed the earlier St. Louis church in 1788?
nola.why: It burned on Good Friday, March 21, 1788.

nola.q: Which roof was added to the Cabildo in 1847?
nola.why: A third floor with a French-style mansard roof.

nola.q: The French Market was dedicated as a market in which year?
nola.why: Part of the space was dedicated as a market in 1791.

detroit.q: What did Diego Rivera paint in the Rivera Court?
detroit.why: He painted the Detroit Industry murals in fresco, 1932 to 1933.

When did Michigan Central Station reopen?

minneapolis.q: What ignited in the 1878 Washburn A Mill explosion?
What was the Stone Arch Bridge built for?
Who wrote a march for Foshay Tower's dedication?
minneapolis.why: Sousa wrote it, and Foshay's check bounced.

minneapolis.q: Spoonbridge and Cherry was installed in which year?
minneapolis.why: It was placed by cranes on May 9, 1988.

atlanta.q: Who was co-pastor at Ebenezer with his father from 1960?
Centennial Olympic Park was built for which Games?
What campaign saved the Atlanta Fox in 1974?
atlanta.why: Save the Fox formed after a demolition plan.

atlanta.q: What year did Oakland Cemetery begin?
atlanta.why: It began in 1850 as Atlanta Cemetery.

memphis.q: What did Congress call Beale Street in 1977?
How much did Elvis pay for Graceland?
How many Mallards march at the Peabody?

savannah.q: When was the Forsyth Park fountain installed?
The cathedral was rebuilt after a fire in which year?
savannah.why: Fire destroyed the interior on February 6, 1898.

savannah.q: Which Declaration signer is buried at Colonial Park?
What trade built River Street's warehouses?
savannah.why: Cotton brokers, called factors, worked there.
